items.meaning: friend; a person linked to another by friendship
items.reviewNote: Mon ami is a friendly form of address to the philosopher. The proper global ami friendship owner and all three amis banks were read, excluding the female-friend-only sense. Add the singular surface to the same friendship meaning; ami/ennemi/inconnu/adversaire are masculine singular nouns after mon. Contextual address does not establish an intimate historical relationship or create a separate vocative sense.

items.meaning: Leibnizian; an adherent of Leibniz’s philosophy
items.reviewNote: Un Leibnitzien and le Leibnitzien name a person adhering to Leibniz’s philosophy, not an adjective modifying another noun. No proper global or earlier leibnitzien/leibnizien owner was found. Prepare the proper French leibnizien noun, preserving historical t and source capitalization as surface variants rather than fresh meanings. All four philosophical-follower nouns are masculine singular after un. The mechanical analogies are the character’s account, not a verified statement of the whole doctrine.

items.meaning: hand; the pointer on a clock dial
items.reviewNote: Une aiguille qui montre les heures is the clock hand in the soul analogy, not a sewing needle or a watch noun. Académie1762 explicitly records the clock-pointer use. No proper global or earlier aiguille owner exists. Aiguille/cloche/chaîne/bordure are feminine singular nouns after une; the moving pointer differs from a bell, chain or surrounding border. Preserve the general pointer meaning without a soul-only metaphor sense.

items.meaning: chimes; rings out a peal
items.reviewNote: Both carillonne represent the clock’s audible chiming, attributed alternately to soul and body in the analogy. Académie9 records the intransitive bell/clock use separately from proclaiming a news item. Prepare proper French carillonner verb ownership. All four complete singular predicates fit elle; chiming differs from silence, movement or stopping. No soul-only or body-only new meaning is made.

items.meaning: mirror; an image-reflecting object used in a comparison
items.reviewNote: Mon âme est le miroir de l’univers and the later border of that mirror extend a reflecting-object comparison. The complete global physical miroir bank was read; miroir/cadre/portrait/rideau match masculine singular agreement. Add this context bank on the same reflective-object core, with definition-scope review of its narrow glass/crystal/material and small-size wording before import. Do not invent a metaphor-only fresh sense or certify the soul as a material mirror. All new middle alternatives are masculine singular nouns after le.

items.meaning: border; the frame surrounding an object
items.reviewNote: La bordure du miroir names its surrounding frame in the extended soul/body comparison, not decoration unrelated to the edge. No global or earlier proper bordure noun owner exists. Bordure/surface/couleur/épaisseur are feminine singular nouns after sa; encircling the object distinguishes a border from its surface, colour or thickness. Preserve a general surrounding-edge/frame meaning rather than a body-only sense.

items.meaning: clear; easy to understand
items.reviewNote: Cela est clair is the philosopher’s claim that his account is understandable, with contextual irony. No proper global or earlier clair adjective owner was found. The four masculine singular predicates fit c’est. Preserve intelligibility separately from literal light colour or brightness; do not endorse the adequacy of the explanation or create an irony-only sense.

items.meaning: adherent; a supporter of a doctrine
items.reviewNote: Un petit partisan de Locke names a follower of Locke’s philosophical position, not an armed irregular fighter or the adjective biased. No proper earlier/global partisan owner exists. Partisan/opposant/ennemi/détracteur are masculine singular nouns after un; support contrasts with opposition, enmity or detraction. A particular philosopher does not create a new scene-only meaning.

items.meaning: nearby; close at hand
items.reviewNote: Là tout auprès stands alone as an adverb meaning nearby, without a de complement. The exact preposition bank and global proper auprès adverb with historical auprés surface were read in all three bands. Add the modern surface on the same existing nearby meaning, not a spelling-only sense. All four spatial adverbs fit il reste; nearby differs from remoteness, elsewhere or outside. Before import compare duplicated preposition/adverb families under correct ownership, keeping unrelated démarches auprès de separate.

items.meaning: had; auxiliary forming a completed past
items.reviewNote: Eut adressé and eut ouvert form completed past constructions, not possession, receiving an order or an independent lexical had. The exact mixed possession/auxiliary bank and earlier received-order bank were read alongside the proper global compound-auxiliary family and three banks. Add this surface on the same existing auxiliary sense without a past-anterior-only identity. The middle clue explicitly tests auxiliary function; the four autonymous past forms differ in lexical function. Preserve the shared auxiliary meaning and historical mastery.

items.meaning: think; form thoughts or judgments
items.reviewNote: Comment je pense asks about mental activity; plus de choses possibles qu’on ne pense refers to judgment or belief. Both fit the existing broad forming-thought/reflection/judgment definition. The earlier IV pense bank and global pensé three bands were read. Add this surface on the same proper penser meaning; no belief-only or first-person-only fresh sense. The earlier IV middle options redundantly include object clitics after je le and require whole-work bank repair/normalization before import. All new singular predicates fit je and differ semantically; present and past surfaces share mastery by sense.

items.meaning: immaterial; having no material or bodily nature
items.reviewNote: Immatérielles qualifies the hypothesized substances as nonmaterial, rather than unimportant in an English idiom. No proper global or earlier French immatériel adjective exists. All four feminine plural predicates agree with substances; nonmaterial nature contrasts with material, bodily or physical nature. Preserve proper French ownership without a gender-only meaning, and keep the speaker’s assertion distinct from established fact.

items.meaning: intelligent; capable of understanding and reasoning
items.reviewNote: Substances intelligentes predicates capacity for thought, not a separate feminine-only sense or an IQ claim. The earlier VI intelligents bank was read in all bands. Add this feminine plural surface on the same proper intelligent adjective meaning. All four feminine plural choices agree with substances and contrast mental capacity with inertness, unconsciousness or absence of reflection. The characters’ immaterial-substance claim is not certified.

items.meaning: impart; transmit a faculty or property
items.reviewNote: Communiquer la pensée à la matière means imparting the faculty of thinking, not merely exchanging information with another speaker. The earlier II communiqué and VI communiquer information-sharing banks were read. Académie8 distinguishes transmission of a quality, power or movement from making information known. Prepare this impart-property meaning under the same planned proper communiquer verb lemma, with explicit comparison against the broad transmission core before import and no infinitive-only sense. All infinitives take la lui; transmission contrasts with denial, removal or prohibition. The bank does not establish the theological claim as fact.

items.meaning: revere; regard with profound respect
items.reviewNote: Je révère la puissance éternelle expresses reverence for the deity’s power, not merely noticing it or reporting a fact. No proper earlier/global révérer verb was found. Every first-person singular predicate takes je la; profound respect contrasts with contempt, insult or ridicule. Preserve the general reverence meaning without a deity-only sense.

items.meaning: eternal; without beginning or end
items.reviewNote: Puissance éternelle attributes timeless existence to the same deity as earlier l’Être éternel. The complete earlier VII éternel bank and all three questions were read. Add this feminine surface on the same planned proper éternel adjective sense; all four predicates agree with puissance. Source theological conception is reported, not certified, and grammatical gender creates no fresh meaning.

items.meaning: is for someone to; is their place or responsibility to
items.reviewNote: Il ne m’appartient pas de la borner denies that limiting divine power is the speaker’s place or right. The global group-membership and property-ownership families plus earlier VI/VII property banks were compared. Académie1762 explicitly records impersonal right, duty or propriety. Prepare this impersonal responsibility/right meaning on the existing proper appartenir verb, rather than ownership, with no tense-only sense. The middle clue is metalinguistic and all four alternatives are singular verbs; responsibility/right differs from an event happening, importance or something escaping attention.

items.meaning: limit; set bounds to
items.reviewNote: La borner sets bounds to the eternal power, rather than erecting a literal fence or a narrowly topographical boundary. No proper earlier/global borner owner exists. Prepare a general limiting-extent verb meaning covering abstract scope; every infinitive takes la. Limitation contrasts with extension, increase or multiplication. Negation does not create a separate meaning or approve the theological argument.

items.meaning: am content with; limit myself to without seeking more
items.reviewNote: Je me contente de croire is a pronominal contenter verb with an infinitive complement, not the feminine content adjective. Académie1762 records remaining with what one has done and doing no more. No global/earlier proper contenter owner exists. Prepare that verb meaning under proper French contenter. All four first-person pronominal predicates take de le croire; accepting a limit contrasts with avoidance, restraint or haste. Existing content adjective ownership and mastery remain separate.

items.meaning: possible; capable of existing or occurring
items.reviewNote: Choses possibles identifies what can exist or occur, not probable outcomes or certainty. The complete global possible adjective definition and three banks were read. Add the plural surface on the same existing meaning; the potential existence scope should be expressed alongside realizability at whole-family import without a plural-only or philosophy-only sense. All four feminine plural predicates agree with choses.

items.meaning: would have; auxiliary of a hypothetical completed action
items.reviewNote: Aurait embrassé is a hypothetical completed-action auxiliary, not the exact published lexical conditional-possession bank. The full exact bank and global compound-auxiliary three bands were read, with earlier VII auraient compared. Add this surface on the same proper auxiliary meaning without a conditional-only identity. The metalinguistic middle clue selects auxiliary have from four singular conditional forms; be, want and can do not supply that function. The narrative does not say the embrace actually occurred.

items.meaning: embraced; held someone affectionately or kissed them
items.reviewNote: The proposed embrace is an affectionate gesture prevented by the extreme size disparity, not embracing a doctrine intellectually. The proper global affectionate embrasser meaning and all three existing embrassant bands were read. Add the participial surface on that same broad embrace/kiss meaning; the text does not resolve the precise gesture beyond affection. All singular participles fit il l’aurait and contrast affection with rejection, insult or avoidance. No participle-only meaning or actually-performed action is asserted.

items.meaning: follower; an adherent of a doctrine
items.reviewNote: Le sectateur de Locke names the same doctrine follower as partisan, with a separate French lexical head rather than shared ownership under partisan. No earlier/global proper sectateur noun exists. Sectateur/opposant/ennemi/détracteur are masculine singular nouns after son; doctrine adherence contrasts with opposition, enmity or detraction. Preserve the general historical follower meaning without limiting it to one philosopher or a modern cult accusation.

items.meaning: extreme; reaching a very great degree
items.reviewNote: L’extrême disproportion qualifies the very great degree of size mismatch, not an extremity noun or a separate feminine sense. No proper earlier/global extrême adjective exists. All four invariable singular predicates agree with disproportion and differ semantically in degree. No source measurement beyond the stated enormous disparity is certified.

items.meaning: disproportion; a marked mismatch in relative scale
items.reviewNote: The disproportion between the dwarf and the human prevents the embrace; it is a lack of compatible relative scale, not merely any small difference. No proper earlier/global disproportion noun exists. Disproportion/similitude/égalité/équivalence are feminine singular nouns after une; great scale mismatch contrasts with similarity or equivalent/equal measure. Preserve a general lack-of-proportion meaning rather than an embrace-only sense.

items.meaning: animalcule; a minute animal or tiny being
items.reviewNote: Un petit animalcule labels the tiny philosopher from the giants’ perspective, metaphorically using the minute-animal noun. No proper earlier/global animalcule owner exists. Animalcule/colosse/géant/titan are masculine singular nouns after un and contrast minute with gigantic scale. The plural animalcules shares this same planned noun meaning; no modern species classification or human-specific fresh sense is asserted.

items.meaning: animalcules; minute animals or tiny beings
items.reviewNote: Animalcules philosophes names the other minute humans in the same tiny-animal comparison. Share the current singular animalcule bank’s proper planned noun meaning, with explicit same-package owner and no plural-only fresh meaning. Animalcules/colosses/géants/titans are masculine plural nouns after des; minute rather than gigantic scale selects the answer. Philosophes is the following characterization, not a modern biological classification.

items.meaning: knew; possessed knowledge of
items.reviewNote: Il dit qu’il savait tout le secret is the pedant’s claim to knowledge, not know-how or inability in ne saurait. The global broad know bank and earlier VII su three bands were read. Add the imperfect surface on that same proper savoir knowledge meaning; normalize old present-only naming/metadata before import without a tense-only sense. All singular predicates take la; knowledge differs from forgetting, ignorance or denial, and the claim is not independently certified.

items.meaning: secret; hidden knowledge or explanation
items.reviewNote: Tout le secret means hidden knowledge of the subjects being debated, not the detention isolation in au secret or the adjective concealed. The exact isolation bank and global hidden-information secrets bank were read in all three bands. Add singular secret on the same hidden-knowledge core, with shared definition-scope review to include an unknown explanation rather than only deliberately confidential information before import. Secret/communiqué/ordre/salut are masculine singular nouns after un; hidden rather than announced, commanded or greeted selects secret. No philosophy-only fresh meaning is made.

items.meaning: summa; a comprehensive work on a field of knowledge
items.reviewNote: La Somme de saint Thomas names the comprehensive theological work, not a sum of money, numerical addition or a nap. The exact money bank and global arithmetic family were compared in all relevant bands. Académie9 explicitly lists the comprehensive literary work under the same feminine somme noun and names Thomas’s title. Prepare this work/compendium meaning on the existing proper feminine somme owner; title capitalization creates no fresh identity. Somme/notice/lettre/liste are feminine singular nouns after une; breadth and synthesis distinguish a summa from a brief document or mere list. The character’s claim that all answers are contained there is not certified.

items.meaning: saint; holy, as a religious qualification before a name
items.reviewNote: Saint before Thomas is a religious adjective qualifying the named person, rather than the name Thomas itself or a stand-alone saint noun. Académie9 lists named saints such as saint Pierre and saint Augustin in its adjective section; nominal saints have a separate section. No proper earlier/global saint owner exists. Prepare proper French saint adjective ownership and general religious-sanctity meaning, without a title-only or masculine-only sense. All four masculine singular adjectives are compatible with the metalinguistic clue, contrasting religious sanctity with profane, impious or secular status.

items.meaning: looked at; directed his gaze toward
items.reviewNote: Il regarda names the act of looking at the two visitors; the exact separate de haut en bas expression supplies contempt. The proper global looking verb and all three regardait banks were read. Add the past-simple surface on that same meaning, preserving the phrase’s independent span and suppressing only its components. All four predicates fit il les; visual gaze differs from hearing, avoidance or forgetting. No contempt-only or past-simple-only regarder sense is made.

items.meaning: celestial; belonging to the sky or heavens
items.reviewNote: Les habitants célestes are the two visitors from other celestial bodies, not necessarily angels or morally heavenly beings. No proper earlier/global céleste adjective owner exists. All four masculine plural predicates agree with habitants and contrast heavenly/celestial with earthly, underground or aquatic origin. Preserve the general sky/heavens meaning without a visitor-specific fresh sense.

items.meaning: maintained; asserted and defended a claim
items.reviewNote: Il leur soutint que... maintains the pedant’s assertion that everything was created for humans, not physical support of a body. No proper earlier/global soutenir verb exists. All four singular past predicates take la. Assertion and defense contrast with denial, forgetting or concealment; prepare the generic maintaining-claim meaning without a theology-only sense and without certifying the claim.

items.meaning: persons; individuals considered in their own right
items.reviewNote: Leurs personnes refers to the two extraterrestrial visitors as individual persons, not the negative pronoun nobody. The proper global personne noun and all three exact personnes banks were read. Add this context bank on the same individual-person core, with explicit whole-family definition-scope review of its human-only wording before import; do not create an extraterrestrial-only meaning. Personnes/chaises/tables/maisons are feminine plural nouns after des. The narrative treats the visitors as persons without asserting real extraterrestrial life.

items.meaning: worlds; celestial realms or inhabited globes
items.reviewNote: Leurs mondes are the visitors’ celestial worlds or globes, contrasted with their suns and stars. The global proper monde human-society, all-people and negative-emphasis families were compared; none owns this cosmic scope. Prepare the world-as-celestial-domain meaning under the existing French monde noun, not a new plural-only owner. Mondes/océans/continents/royaumes are masculine plural nouns after leurs; complete celestial globes differ from their geographic or political subdivisions. The claimed human-centered purpose is reported rather than endorsed.

items.meaning: suns; luminous stars of planetary systems
items.reviewNote: Leurs soleils extends sun to the luminous stellar bodies of the visitors’ worlds. The global soleil star family and three banks were read. Add the plural surface on the same sun/star core; broaden the Earth-only definition scope after full current/historical impact before import, not a plural-only fresh meaning. Soleils/satellites/nuages/rochers are masculine plural nouns after leurs and distinguish luminous stars from orbiting bodies, atmospheric clouds or rocks. No modern catalog of planetary systems is asserted.

items.meaning: solely; exclusively
items.reviewNote: Uniquement pour l’homme restricts the asserted purpose to humans alone. No proper earlier/global uniquement owner exists. All four adverbs fit pour lui and contrast total exclusivity with partial, principal or additional inclusion. Prepare the general solely/exclusively meaning without a theology-only sense and without verifying the assertion.

items.meaning: choking; struggling to breathe, here from excessive laughter
items.reviewNote: En étouffant de ce rire describes breathlessness from excessive laughter, not the transitive suppression of a truth or proof or concealment of laughter. The proper global étouffer suppression family and three bands were read. Académie1835 records étouffer de rire as laughing until losing breath. Prepare the intransitive struggle-to-breathe meaning under the same proper étouffer verb, not a participle-only or laughter-only owner. All complete participial choices fit en. The source is humorous hyperbole rather than a medical diagnosis.

items.meaning: laughter; an audible expression of amusement
items.reviewNote: Ce rire inextinguible is a masculine singular noun, not the exact published infinitive rire. The complete exact verb bank and global/earlier proper lemma inventory were read; only verb owners exist. Prepare proper French rire noun ownership, keeping the verb separate rather than attaching a noun to it. Rire/sanglot/cri/soupir are masculine singular nouns after ce. Gaiety distinguishes laughter from sobbing, crying out or sighing, and no deity-only meaning is made.

items.meaning: inextinguishable; impossible to quench or stop
items.reviewNote: Inextinguible qualifies laughter that cannot be stopped. Académie9 explicitly includes figurative irrepressible laughter alongside unquenchable fire/thirst, including a Homeric example. No proper earlier/global inextinguible owner exists. Prepare the broad unquenchable/unstoppable adjective meaning without a laughter-only or Homer-only identity. All masculine singular predicates agree with rire and contrast persistence with brevity, interruption or transience; no exact classical quotation is asserted.

items.meaning: gods; divine beings in mythology
items.reviewNote: Des dieux names the mythological gods mentioned in the Homeric allusion, rather than using Dieu as an excluded proper name. The proper global dieu deity meaning and all three divine-being banks were read. Add the plural surface on the same existing meaning; dieux/rois/marins/prêtres are masculine plural nouns after les. Divinity distinguishes gods from rulers, sailors and cult officiants. Plural morphology and a specific mythology create no fresh meaning.

items.meaning: bellies; the abdominal regions
items.reviewNote: Leurs ventres names the bodily abdominal regions shaken by laughter. The earlier VII ventre maternal-womb context bank was read in all bands. Add the plural surface to that same general belly/abdominal-region meaning, rather than create a separate male, plural or laughter-only sense. Before import normalize the earlier learner gloss beyond the maternal context while preserving its exact questions. Ventres/mentons/genoux/coudes are masculine plural nouns after leurs; the trunk region differs from the lower face or limb joints.

items.meaning: convulsions; involuntary bodily spasms or jerks
items.reviewNote: Ces convulsions refers to abrupt bodily shakes under uncontrollable laughter, not necessarily a diagnosed disease or a political upheaval. No proper earlier/global convulsion noun exists. Convulsions/caresses/pauses/postures are feminine plural nouns after des; involuntary jerking differs from touch, rest or a sustained bodily position. Preserve the general spasm/jerk meaning without a laughter-only or plural-only sense.

items.meaning: fell; dropped downward
items.reviewNote: The vessel drops from the Sirian’s nail into the Saturnian’s pocket. The proper global physical tomber fall family and all three banks were read, alongside earlier IV tombèrent. Add the past-simple surface to the same physical fall meaning, not a ship-only or tense-only sense. All singular past predicates fit il y; downward falling differs from ascent, floating or remaining. The source span and occurrence are unchanged.
